neighbours.label: the suffix piece 'er' when it splits off as its own token (comparatives and agent nouns: pal|er, round|er, hear|er)
fire: Compared with its sister species, this finch has a paler beak.
With age the old stone arch looks rounder at the edges.
Each listener and hearer in the crowd took something different from the speech.
Under this lamp her skin seemed paler than it did at noon.
The sculptor kept shaping the clay until the bowl grew rounder.
A careful hearer can tell when a speaker is unsure.
By autumn the leaves on that hedge turn paler and then fall.
The second loaf came out rounder because of the new tin.
quiet: Compared with its sister species, this finch has a pale beak.
With age the old stone arch looks smooth at the edges.
Each child and parent in the crowd took something different from the speech.
Under this lamp her skin seemed pale as it did at noon.
The sculptor kept shaping the clay until the bowl grew round.
A careful person can tell when a speaker is unsure.
By autumn the leaves on that hedge turn pale and then fall.
The second loaf came out round because of the new tin.
